data.situation: Upstairs, the blue cup appeared again, this time behind glass. Bowls and small jugs stood beside it: ceramics from a pottery that had once supplied the market. Each artefact had a number linked to the gallery's collection records. A label identified the pieces as authentic objects donated by a former worker's family. Arthur studied the cup's handle. It looked familiar, but he could not say who had made this particular one. Maya wanted to see the mark underneath. She could not turn the cup in the case, but a tablet beside it showed digital replicas of the objects. A volunteer named Jo showed her how to rotate the image. The mark came into view, then the handle. “That is the copy on the screen,” Jo said. “The original stays here so we can preserve it.” Maya looked from the glowing image to the quiet row behind the glass. Near the window, Jo offered them tea in ordinary paper cups. Arthur laughed at the difference. The old cups were not there for visitors to drink from, however familiar they seemed. Maya could turn the replicas on screen to see the shapes, then look at the originals without handling them. She asked about their weight. Jo said the screen could not give her that feeling, and they left the question open. At the exit, a box held cards headed “A memory of the market”. They were part of the gallery's public engagement with local history; visitors could leave a memory or a question if they wished. Arthur wrote about the cups on his mother's stall, then added, “I do not know whether these came from the same pottery.” Jo put the card among the accounts waiting to be checked. Outside, Maya asked him what else he remembered, and he began with the smell of wet canvas after rain.
data.easySummary: The cups upstairs are original ceramics. Maya uses digital replicas to see their shapes without handling the objects. The gallery keeps them in a case to preserve them. Arthur leaves a personal memory, clearly saying what he does not know.
data.easySummaryZh: 楼上的杯子是原来的陶瓷制品。玛雅借助数字复制品观察形状，而不拿起器物。美术馆把原物留在展柜中保存。阿瑟留下一段个人回忆，也明确说出自己不知道的部分。

glossary.note: 复数名词，指用黏土制成并经加热变硬的物品。这里是杯、碗等制品，不是陶瓷制造学科。
glossary.example: The case holds ceramics from a local pottery.
glossary.exampleZh: 展柜里放着来自当地陶器作坊的陶瓷制品。

externalEvidence.definition: an artifact made of hard brittle material produced from nonmetallic minerals by firing at high temperatures
externalEvidence.limitationZh: explicit lemma ceramic；复数器物不同于ceramics同形精确词条的制作学科。WN原义不只限于黏土，不将作者具体材料扩写进原定义。

glossary.zh: 人工制品；有文化或历史意义的人造物
glossary.note: 可数名词；英式拼写artefact。杯是人制作的器物，不能因为它小或日常就排除在artefact概念之外；并非所有人造物都是珍贵文物。
glossary.example: A cup used in daily life can also be an artefact in a gallery collection.
glossary.exampleZh: 日常使用的杯子也可以作为馆藏中的一件人工制品。

externalEvidence.supportParaphraseZh: 人造物，尤其具历史或文化价值的物件；artifact为尤其北美英语的异体拼写。
externalEvidence.limitationZh: Selected dictionary sense/pattern only, not corpus-frequency evidence or whole dictionary import. 项目例句原创，没有复制商用例句。

externalEvidence.definition: a man-made object taken as a whole
externalEvidence.limitationZh: 英式lemma原索引真实存在；不强制改为artifact；历史珍贵性不是WN此义必要条件。

glossary.note: 形容词；本课由展签与收藏记录表明为原物，不能只凭裂痕或旧外观鉴定。与复制品区分，不选择authentic的仿真模型义。
glossary.example: The label identifies the cups as authentic pieces from the former pottery.
glossary.exampleZh: 展签说明这些杯子是原先陶器作坊留下的真品。

externalEvidence.supportParaphraseZh: 第一义真品而非复制品；第三义仿照原物制作的逼真之物不是本课所选义。
externalEvidence.limitationZh: Selected dictionary sense/pattern only, not corpus-frequency evidence or whole dictionary import. 项目例句原创，没有复制商用例句。
展签说明原物身份，不能以外观或个人记忆判断；不将可靠事实义用于物件真假。

glossary.note: 复数名词短语；本课为记录展品形状的屏幕模型，不是手里可拿的原物，也不保证保留所有材料、重量或历史。
glossary.example: The digital replicas let visitors turn the cups on screen without touching the originals.
glossary.exampleZh: 数字复制品让来客在屏幕上旋转杯子，而不用碰原物。

externalEvidence.supportParaphraseZh: replica为十分接近或准确的复制品。
externalEvidence.limitationZh: 只支持replica组成词；digital replicas整块来源为R01179，项目用平板上的可转动模型具体化，不能把组成词页面冒充整块词典条目。 项目例句原创，没有复制商用例句。

glossary.note: 及物动词；preserve something表示保存、保护某物，使它免于损坏。这里原物留在展柜内，数字复制品用于查看。
glossary.example: The gallery keeps the old cups in the case to preserve them.
glossary.exampleZh: 美术馆把旧杯子留在展柜里保存。

externalEvidence.definition: keep in safety and protect from harm, decay, loss, or destruction
externalEvidence.limitationZh: 展示隔离保护器物及旧信，原义v02679899保持状态也相关，保留为可用备选；不把陈列安排说成通用修复程序。

glossary.note: 名词短语；参观者可自愿提供记忆与问题，工作人员仍须区分个人回忆与已核史实。不是订婚或一场军事交战。
glossary.example: The memory cards are one way to encourage public engagement with local history.
glossary.exampleZh: 回忆卡是一种鼓励公众参与地方历史的方式。

externalEvidence.supportParaphraseZh: 不可数正式名词，指为理解人与事而参与；不选订婚、预约或军事交战义。
externalEvidence.limitationZh: 只支持engagement参与义及with/in结构；public engagement整块来源为R01165，不把单词条目冒充整块条目。 项目例句原创，没有复制商用例句。

glossary.note: preserve接所保存的对象，不等于随意修补或翻新。

retrievalPrompts.cue: Describe the objects in the case. The label and collection records identify them as original pieces from the former pottery; Arthur only says they look familiar.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 描述展柜里的物件。展签与收藏记录说明它们是原先陶器作坊的原物；阿瑟只是觉得眼熟。
acceptableAnswers: These are ceramics, and each is an artefact in the collection. The label identifies them as authentic pieces; Arthur's memory alone does not establish that.
checks: 不凭旧外观或眼熟自行鉴定

retrievalPrompts.cue: Maya wants to see a mark under a cup, but cannot turn the original. Explain how she can see it and why the cup stays in the case.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 玛雅想看杯底标记，却不能翻动原杯。说明怎样查看，以及杯子为什么留在展柜里。
acceptableAnswers: She can turn the digital replicas on screen. The authentic objects stay in the case so the gallery can preserve them.
checks: 不声称屏幕提供重量或完整材料体验

retrievalPrompts.cue: Arthur remembers cups on his mother's stall, but does not know whether they came from the same pottery. Explain how his card contributes to the gallery and what needs to remain uncertain.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 阿瑟记得母亲摊位上的杯子，却不知道那些杯子是否来自同一家作坊。说明他的卡片怎样帮助美术馆，以及哪些信息仍不确定。
acceptableAnswers: His card supports public engagement with local history. It records a personal memory, but the link to this pottery still needs to be checked.
checks: 个人回忆与已核史实分开
参与自愿，不要求私人资料

transferPrompt.cue: An archive shows an old letter behind glass and a digital copy beside it. A visitor remembers a similar envelope at home but cannot identify this letter. Explain why the copy is useful, why the original stays protected and how the visitor can contribute without guessing.
transferPrompt.cueZh: 一处档案展把旧信放在玻璃后，旁边提供数字复制品。来客记得家里有过类似信封，却无法认定这封信。说明复制品为什么有用、原物为何保留保护，以及来客怎样在不猜测的情况下提供帮助。
acceptableAnswers: A digital replica helps visitors inspect details while the archive preserves the original. Public engagement can include a personal memory with its limits clearly stated; a similar envelope does not identify this letter.
checks: 不把相似当作身份或真伪证明
